articles.title: Dupla é condenada a 171 anos de prisão por atirar contra jovens no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: João Batista Severino e Sebastião Rodrigues Cordeiro receberam penas de 85 anos e 10 meses de prisão cada um, em regime inicial fechado, pelo crime cometido em 2011.
articles.summary: João Batista Severino e Sebastião Rodrigues Cordeiro receberam penas de 85 anos e 10 meses de prisão cada um, em regime inicial fechado, pelo crime cometido em 2011.
articles.body:
Ministério Público do Espírito Santo (MPES) — Foto: TV Gazeta

Uma dupla de comerciantes foi condenada a 171 anos de prisão por matar um jovem, tentar matar outros dois e balear uma menina, em Vitória . Segundo a acusação, os condenados confundiram os três homens com assaltantes e abriram fogo contra o grupo, atingindo também a criança de 11 anos.

O julgamento terminou na noite de quinta-feira (19). João Batista Severino e Sebastião Rodrigues Cordeiro receberam penas de 85 anos e 10 meses de prisão cada um, em regime inicial fechado, com três qualificadoras: motivo torpe, perigo comum e recurso que dificultou a defesa das vítimas .

O crime aconteceu no bairro São Pedro I, em Vitória, na noite de 12 de abril de 2011. Três jovens caminhavam pela Rua da Paz quando foram surpreendidos por disparos. Maxwel Paulino foi atingido e morreu, já Evandro Paulino dos Santos e Luiz Carlos Paulino conseguiram escapar.

A menina de 11 anos, que não fazia parte do grupo e passava pela rua no momento, também foi baleada, mas sobreviveu.

De acordo com a denúncia do Ministério Público do Espírito Santo (MPES), os acusados eram comerciantes da região e suspeitavam que os jovens fossem responsáveis por assaltos registrados pouco antes na localidade.

Ainda segundo a acusação, João Batista dirigia um Volkswagen Gol branco, enquanto Sebastião estava no banco do passageiro. Ao avistarem os jovens, eles se aproximaram.

Sebastião desceu do veículo e efetuou diversos disparos contra o grupo. Depois, ainda atirou na direção de uma das vítimas que tentava fugir.

O MPES sustentou que o ataque repentino impediu que as vítimas se defendessem. Além disso, os tiros foram disparados em uma rua estreita e cercada por residências, colocando outras pessoas em risco.

Até a publicação desta reportagem, o g1 não localizou a defesa de João Batista Severino e Sebastião Rodrigues Cordeiro.

articles.title: Even €300M isn’t enough: Bayern Munich declare €60M signing Michael Olise unsellable despite persistent Real Madrid links
articles.summary: Bayern Munich's president Herbert Hainer insists that star winger Michael Olise is not for sale, even for a record €300 million, amid ongoing interest from Real Madrid. Discover why Olise is central to Bayern's future plans.
articles.body: Real Madrid may have the financial muscle to pursue almost any player in European football, but Bayern Munich have made it clear that Michael Olise is not for sale. Club president Herbert Hainer has dismissed the possibility of accepting even a €300 million offer for the French winger, insisting Bayern would rather build their future around him than turn his performances into a transfer profit. With Olise flourishing in Germany and Real Madrid repeatedly linked with him, Hainer has also offered an important clarification about the Spanish club's interest.Bayern Munich reject €300m offer for Michael OliseSpeaking to German publication t-online, Hainer ruled out selling Olise regardless of the size of a potential offer, making clear that Bayern have no intention of negotiating his departure.“We are not a selling club, we are a buying club,” Hainer said, echoing a familiar stance previously expressed by former Bayern chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. The Bayern president stressed that the club's approach had not changed, insisting that transfer decisions could not be judged purely on financial terms.“You can't always just look at the financial aspect. You also have to consider whether the player is a good fit for us – in terms of playing style, personality, character traits, and also as a person,” Hainer explained.His comments underlined Bayern's determination to retain Olise, whose importance to their attacking plans goes beyond his potential transfer value. Hainer also dismissed suggestions that the Frenchman might be tempted to leave the Bundesliga champions, adding: “Michael feels at home here and knows what he has at FC Bayern.”The 24-year-old France international is contracted to Bayern until June 2029, and his agreement contains no release clause. That leaves the German club in a strong position to resist approaches, with Hainer confident that Olise has little reason to seek an exit.Herbert Hainer reveals what Florentino Perez told him about Real MadridReal Madrid have repeatedly been linked with Olise, with reports suggesting the Spanish giants pursued the winger during the previous summer transfer window. Hainer has now provided his account of a conversation with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, which took place when the Bayern chief attended a graduation ceremony at the Spanish club's university school.According to Hainer, Perez assured him that Real Madrid had never held discussions with Olise or his representatives about a potential transfer.“He assured me that Real Madrid had never held talks with Michael Olise or his agent,” Hainer said.The comments challenge speculation that negotiations had taken place between the Spanish club and the player's camp, although they do not rule out Real Madrid's admiration for the winger or future interest.Hainer had already taken a firm position in June 2026, when he publicly addressed the possibility of an approach from Perez.“If Florentino wants to send us an offer, which has not happened to date, he can save himself the trouble,” he said.His latest comments leave little ambiguity about Bayern's intentions: Olise is regarded as a player to build around, not an asset the club is prepared to sell, even for a fee that would rank among the biggest in football history. Hainer also highlighted the quality of Bayern's attack, declaring that the club currently have one of the best attacking trios in world football with Harry Kane, Olise and Luis Díaz.Michael Olise's Bayern Munich career, trophies and individual awardsOlise joined Bayern from Crystal Palace on July 7, 2024, for a reported €60 million, approximately $65 million, including add-ons. He signed a five-year contract running until June 30, 2029, and has since developed into one of the most productive players in the Bundesliga.Across 122 appearances in all competitions, the Frenchman has recorded 54 goals and 55 assists, averaging almost one direct goal contribution per appearance. His influence has extended beyond individual numbers, with Bayern winning consecutive Bundesliga titles in 2024-25 and 2025-26.Olise also helped the club win the DFB-Pokal in 2025-26 and the 2025 German Supercup, bringing his major domestic trophy collection with Bayern to four. He was named Bayern's Player of the Season in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, won the 2025-26 Bundesliga Player of the Season award and finished ninth in the 2026 Ballon d'Or voting.His development in Germany followed three seasons at Crystal Palace, where he scored 16 goals in 90 appearances between 2021 and 2024. He had previously progressed through Reading's youth system before establishing himself in English football, making his move to Palace an important step towards the player Bayern eventually signed.Olise's rise has also strengthened his standing with France, where he has become an established international option. At 24, he is already a major part of Bayern's present and long-term plans, which explains why Hainer is so reluctant to entertain the possibility of selling him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roy Coyle: Legendary Irish League manager dies aged 80
articles.summary: The Irish League's most successful manager Roy Coyle dies at the age of 80.
articles.body:
Roy Coyle, the most successful manager in Irish League history, has died at the age of 80.

Coyle won 13 league titles during his 32-year managerial career, achieving periods of sustained success with Linfield and Glentoran.

He also managed Ards, Derry City and Newry City and had a spell as Glentoran director of football.

In a statement, Glentoran said the club were "deeply saddened to announce the passing of Roy Coyle, our former player and manager and one of the greatest figures in our history".

"A league champion in Glentoran colours, Roy went on to become the most successful manager in the club's history. His association with the Oval spanned more than half a century," their statement continued.

"His teams gave supporters some of their most treasured days, while his influence on players and colleagues endured long after his years in the dugout.

"To generations of the Glentoran family, he remained simply 'The Gaffer'."

A minute's applause was held in Coyle's memory before Glentoran's Irish Premiership game against Cliftonville on Friday at Solitude.

Belfast native Coyle moved into management at the age of 29 when he was appointed player-manager of Linfield in November 1975.

A midfielder during his playing days, Coyle had spells with the Glens, Sheffield Wednesday, Grimsby Town and Linfield after starting out with Ballymena United, and he also won five caps for Northern Ireland.

During his 15 years as Blues boss, Coyle won 31 trophies, guiding the club to 10 league titles in just 12 seasons, alongside two Irish Cup successes and an All-Ireland crown in 1981.

"Everyone at Linfield Football Club is deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player and manager, Roy Coyle," the club said.

"His remarkable achievements and contribution to one of the most successful periods in Linfield's history will forever be recognised and remembered.

"The thoughts and deepest condolences of everyone at Linfield Football Club are with Roy's family, friends and all who knew him at this sad time."

After his contract was terminated by Linfield in 1990, Coyle had a spell in the League of Ireland with Derry City between two stints at Ards.

In 1997, he took over at Glentoran and transformed their fortunes, leading the east Belfast club to three league titles and four Irish Cups.

Coyle went on to become the most successful in Glentoran's history, winning 17 trophies before his nine-year tenure at the Oval came to an end in 2006.

He had a brief period in charge of Newry City and also returned for three spells as caretaker boss of Glentoran before retiring in 2017.

'One of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history'

Glentoran chairman Colin Jess paid tribute to Coyle, who was inducted into the club's Hall of Fame in 2025.

"Roy was one of the greatest figures in Glentoran's history, and his passing is a profound loss for our club," said Jess.

"He gave generations of supporters some of the happiest days of their lives. People will always remember where they were and who they were with when his teams won those championships and cups. That is a wonderful thing to have given so many people.

"He set high standards and earned lasting respect. His former players continued to call him The Gaffer long after their playing days had ended, and that says so much about his influence and the place he held in their lives."

Jess added: "We will miss seeing Roy at the ground, enjoying his company and talking football with him. It is difficult to imagine the Oval without him.

"Our deepest sympathy goes to Abbie, the whole family and all those closest to Roy. We are immensely grateful for everything he gave Glentoran, and we will remember him with great affection and pride."

Glentoran owner Ali Pour described Coyle's contribution to Glentoran as "extraordinary".

"He helped make the club champions as a player, led it through years of success as manager and continued to serve it long afterwards," added Pour.

"I often asked Roy for his advice on matters at the club. He knew Glentoran so well, and I valued his judgement and hearing how he saw things. I'll miss those conversations.

"The pride with which supporters remember his teams, and the affection his former players have for him, show how deeply his work mattered to people.

"We owe Roy a great debt of gratitude. His achievements are an enduring part of Glentoran, and we will ensure that future generations understand what he gave this club and why he meant so much to it.

"My family and I extend our heartfelt condolences to Roy's family, friends and everyone mourning his loss. He will always have an honoured place at the Oval."

Northern Ireland Football League (NIFL) chief executive Gerard Lawlor said Coyle's contribution to football in Northern Ireland "went far beyond the trophies he won".

"He was a man who dedicated so much of his life to our local game, earning enormous respect across the football community, regardless of club loyalties," their statement continued.

"Roy represented the passion, commitment and pride that make Irish League football so special. His passing marks the loss of one of the great characters and personalities of our game, and his legacy will live on for generations."

articles.title: Otro contratiempo para Christensen
articles.standfirst: No se ejercitó este viernes por unas leves molestias en el sóleo y es duda para el domingo
articles.summary: No se ejercitó este viernes por unas leves molestias en el sóleo y es duda para el domingo
articles.body: Christensen sigue viviendo un calvario con las lesiones. El defensa sufre unas leves molestias en el sóleo que le impidieron trabajar este viernes con sus compañeros. Ahora mismo es duda para el encuentro contra el Villarreal del domingo. Precisamente, el danés había recibido el alta médica de su última lesión antes del parón por compromisos internacionales. A primera hora de la tarde, el Barcelona emitió un comunicado explicando las dolencias del internacional. "El jugador del primer equipo Andreas Christensen tiene molestias leves en el sóleo de la pierna izquierda. Es duda para el próximo partido. El tiempo de recuperación dependerá de su evolución", reza el texto. Christensen arrancó la temporada con cierta regularidad y participó en siete de los ocho primeros partidos del equipo. Sin embargo, el 19 de septiembre sufrió una lesión muscular en el recto anterior del cuádriceps izquierdo que le obligó a permanecer cerca de un mes y medio alejado de los terrenos de juego. Antes del parón internacional, el danés entró en la convocatoria para el encuentro contra el Atlético de Madrid en el Metropolitano y llegó a disputar cerca de media hora de encuentro. Su regreso suponía una buena noticia para Hansi Flick, que recuperaba una alternativa más para el eje de la defensa. Sin embargo, ahora las nuevas molestias pueden volver a frenar, por enésima vez, su protagonismo. Desde la temporada 24-25, el defensa está sufriendo especialmente con las lesiones. Incluso, en el último parón, el central renunció a acudir a la convocatoria de Dinamarca porque no se sentía preparado para afrontar compromisos internacional. En esta ocasión, no obstante, no se trata de un problema de especial gravedad. Sin embargo, el margen de recuperación es mínimo. Al Barcelona solo le resta una sesión de entrenamiento antes de recibir al Villarreal.

articles.title: Arsenal: Mikel Arteta warns players over Fantasy Premier League team news leak
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.

The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal 's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.

The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal 's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.

Before Saturday's match at Newcastle , Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he said

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.

"This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.

"Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen."

The Spaniard also said his players are restricted from selecting themselves in their FPL line-ups.

In October, a number of FPL teams connected to staff and players at Chelsea removed striker Joao Pedro from their teams, hinting the Brazilian had sustained an injury.

articles.title: Scottish FA plans for youth should not change to pander to clubs - St Mirren's Craig McLeish
articles.summary: St Mirren manager Craig McLeish says it's "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms.
articles.body:
It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.

Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those plans have been diluted.

And McLeish, who took over at St Mirren earlier this year, commented: "That's damning that he's having to change his plans to pander to clubs who aren't really on board with it and don't really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

"I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They're in jobs, they're all fighting for their clubs.

"But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

"It's the way governance is set up and we've killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they've got self-interest, and there's a lot of self-interest at the top end.

"I just don't see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don't ever see that happening. It's really sad."

After reaching three of the past four major men's tournaments, Scotland struggled in their recent Nations League campaign, while Premiership clubs have missed out on the Champions League proper over the past two seasons.

The SFA had proposed including two under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6% of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

"We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base," 36-year-old McLeish, who worked in St Mirren's youth academy before his current role, said.

"We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And, until you fix that, you can't fix the top end of it.

"It's crazy some of the stuff that's going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There's just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

"In this country, football's everyone's sport and everyone gets access to it, but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you're there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

"We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they're not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

"And you're just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

"Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don't get that right, you're dead. You can't do anything after that point and we don't do it well enough. And you're just chasing yourself and we'll never catch up."

Reporting McLeish's remarks, the Press Association said it had asked the SFA for comment.

They echo those of Dundee head coach Steven Pressley, who said on Thursday that Scotland would benefit from the creation of a national football centre and likened the current structure of the game to building on sand.

articles.title: Celtic's Mika Baur out for around 10 weeks, Martin O'Neill says
articles.summary: Germany midfielder Mika Baur will be out for around 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage, Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says.
articles.body:
Mika Baur will be out for around 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage, Celtic manager Martin O'Neill has revealed.

The 22-year-old twice-capped Germany midfielder went off in the recent 1-0 win at home to Kilmarnock and withdrew from his nation's under-21 squad for this month's international break.

Baur, who moved to Glasgow from Paderborn in August, has made 19 appearances so far this season, scoring four times

"He'll be out for some considerable time," O'Neill explained.

"It's a real shame - he was playing great for us. There's talk about 10 weeks. There's things that he can't do for a while. Foot's in the boot.

"He was on fire. It is a blow. It seemed so innocuous at the time.

"I thought that he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on. He's just gone over on it."

Benjamin Nygren missed the second of Sweden's recent double-header and O'Neill cast doubt on the midfielder's participation in Saturday's home Scottish Premiership meeting with St Mirren (15:00 GMT).

"Nygren didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning - he's got a sore heel," the manager said on Friday. "He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks."

O'Neill 'absolutely looking at players' for January

O'Neill's reigning champions are four points clear at the top of the league, having played a game more than nearest challengers Rangers.

The manager says his side have "got to play better" and "be more aggressive going forward".

On the prospect of January additions, O'Neill added: "We're definitely looking at players, wanting to strengthen the squad, which I think we would have to do.

"When people are fit, we will have numbers. We need a bit of quality.

"It would be lovely if, by January, we still had a chance of qualifying for the knockouts of the Europa League. The next couple of games will probably make that decision for us. Hopefully, it's not the breaking point of getting players in.

"I think that we would be doing something. We're absolutely looking at players now.

"I suppose every single club is doing that. The quicker you could get somebody in the better."

articles.summary: "Nuestro objetivo sigue siendo el mismo: llegar a la Final Four y ganar la Nations League", ha dicho el seleccionador
articles.body: La derrota contra Inglaterra del pasado domingo derivó a España hacia el camino más duro en la Nations League. Los de los Luis de Fuente quedaron segundos en el grupo y ahora el sorteo ha deparado que se tienen que enfrentar a Francia, disputando el partido de vuelta fuera, en los cuartos de final. En el recuerdo está el duelo de semifinales del Mundial en el que La Roja eliminó a los galos y se metió en la final ante Argentina para, posteriormente, proclamarse campeona. Zidane, el seleccionador francés, valoró el encuentro ante España y se centró en lo que está por venir, no en lo que ocurrió el pasado mes de julio. "No se trata de una revancha de la semifinal del Mundial, sino de una competición diferente con un nuevo grupo. Y el objetivo sigue siendo el mismo: llegar a la Final Four y ganar la Nations League", comentó. La ida de esos cuartos de final será el 25 de marzo de 2027 (20:45) y la vuelta el 28 de ese mismo mes (20:45) en terreno galo. La extracción de las bolas en el sorteo también reveló el resto del recorrido hacia la final de la Nations League: España, la vigente campeona del mundo y de Europa, o Francia se cruzarán con Países Bajos o Portugal, mientras que Alemania o Bélgica lo harán contra Inglaterra o Noruega. Eso ya será el 9 o el 10 de junio de 2027. La final se disputará el 13 de junio. Zinedine analizó a la selección española. "Sabíamos que nos iba a tocar un rival fuerte. Será España, la actual campeona del mundo. Los conocemos a la perfección, pero hemos estado observando sus últimos partidos y vamos a analizarlo todo con mi cuerpo técnico. Para llegar lejos en una competición hay que jugar y eliminar a los mejores equipos", dijo. Sobre el combinado galo, Zidane afirmó: "Vamos a seguir de cerca a los jugadores que estuvieron con nosotros en noviembre y al resto para preparar la mejor convocatoria para este bonito reto. Sé que todos tienen partidos importantes con sus clubes y que no volveremos a reunirnos hasta dentro de cuatro meses, pero estoy seguro de que mantendrán esta gran cita en un rincón de su mente para estar preparados en marzo".

articles.title: El Estrasburgo le 'roba' a Vítor Matos al Swansea de Modric
articles.standfirst: El exentrenador de los 'cisnes' sustituye a Hugo Oliveira al frente del equipo francés
articles.summary: El exentrenador de los 'cisnes' sustituye a Hugo Oliveira al frente del equipo francés
articles.body: El Swansea de Luka Modric -el croata es inversor y copropietario del cuadro galés- ha sufrido una baja importante... con el curso empezado. Vítor Emanuel Soares Matos (Vila Nova de Gaia, 1988) abandona el banquillo de los 'cisnes'. El técnico portugués, exayudante de Jürgen Klopp en el Liverpool, sustituye a su compatriota Hugo Oliveira como entrenador del Estrasburgo, de la Ligue 1. Matos, que cogió al equipo vigésimo a mitad de la temporada pasada, había renovado recientemente hasta 2030, por lo que el Swansea recibirá una indemnización por su marcha. Sin embargo, su buen hacer -llegó a situar al Swansea líder de la Segunda inglesa- no ha pasado desapercibido. Ya sonó como posible sustituto de Pierre Sage en el Crystal Palace antes del nombramiento de Thomas Frank y se le vinculó, también, con un hipotético regreso a Portugal, donde ya dirigió al Marítimo. Matos deja al Swansea sexto con 26 puntos, a tres del liderato, y toma las riendas de un Estrasburgo que marcha decimotercero, con 10 puntos, dos por encima del descenso, después de enlazar cinco derrotas en seis partidos con Hugo Oliveira.

articles.title: Man Utd drone incident: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola says filming training sessions by drone should be illegal
articles.summary: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal.
articles.body:
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online.

Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances.

The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action.

Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match.

"The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me.

"Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't.

"It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."

Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match.

"We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola.

"We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now."

Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday.

"They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said.

"Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well."

Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United.

But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign.

"You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games.

"We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways.

"We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday."

articles.title: Chelsea: How Joao Pedro is becoming Blues' most important player
articles.summary: With Joao Pedro missing again for Chelsea on Saturday, BBC Sport looks at the importance of the Brazilian to the Blues.
articles.body:
Who is Chelsea 's most important player?

Cole Palmer and Moises Caicedo are names that would probably feature in any debate, but Joao Pedro's recent absence has certainly strengthened the argument in his favour.

The debate started again among Blues fans over the past couple of weeks following their 1-0 defeat by Sunderland , the latest in a run of poor results without the Brazil striker.

The 25-year-old will miss Leeds United 's visit on Saturday with a thigh injury after Chelsea lost three of their previous four matches without him, although one defeat came in a penalty shootout against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup.

Having suffered a 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham in that run, manager Xabi Alonso has faced criticism over his side's lack of identity and some of his personnel decisions , particularly when attempting to replace Joao Pedro.

Danny Welbeck, who was expected to provide cover after his summer arrival from Brighton , has started only one Premier League match during Joao Pedro's injury absence.

Instead, Pedro Neto has twice been deployed through the middle, in the home win over Manchester United and the defeat by Sunderland , while Morgan Rogers started as the central striker against Spurs .

Striker Emmanuel Emegha, signed from Strasbourg over the summer, hasn't started a league game but has struggled with fitness issues of his own.

The continued absence of Joao Pedro is certainly proving costly before the busy winter schedule, with fifth-placed Chelsea already 11 points behind Premier League leaders Arsenal .

Having been handed both a new contract until 2034 and the number nine shirt vacated by Liam Delap in August, Chelsea regard their £55m signing from Brighton in 2025 as a key figure in Alonso's plans.

Asked about scoring more goals without the striker on Friday, Alonso said: "Yes, we need the whole team for that. It's not just the strikers who can score, we can score in set-pieces from defenders, midfielders, so it's teamwork for sure.

"Joao is an important player but we need to be this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.

"The other players, they need to step up and they need to show that they are ready to compete and ready to play for Chelsea ."

Does the data back up Joao Pedro's importance?

There is little doubt Alonso has suffered when Joao Pedro has been unavailable, as did his predecessors. The numbers are undeniable.

Since the start of the 2025-26 Premier League season, Chelsea have averaged 1.8 goals per game with Joao Pedro, compared to 0.6 without.

Their expected goals (xG) drop from 1.8 per game with him to 1.1 without, highlighting a decline in Chelsea's attacking output rather than simply their finishing.

Chelsea average 4.8 shots on target per game when the Brazilian plays, compared with 3.9 when he does not.

Chelsea have failed to score in only 12.2% of Premier League matches involving him, compared with 71.4% when he has been absent.

Those numbers are also reflected in the results.

Chelsea have lost without scoring in just 7.3% of league games featuring Joao Pedro, compared with 71.4% without him. Three of their Premier League defeats this season were without him, while they have scored in every game that he has featured.

Chelsea's points-per-game average falls from 1.5 to 0.9 when he is unavailable.

Joao Pedro, who has also operated as a number 10 and on the wing for Chelsea , appears to improve the output of those around him.

During the past season and a half, Palmer has played 2,317 Premier League minutes alongside him and 528 without him.

Palmer has scored 12 goals and registered four assists with the Brazil forward in the side, equating to 0.6 goal involvements per 90 minutes. Without him, Palmer has managed one goal and no assists, equivalent to 0.2 goal involvements per 90.

Palmer's chance creation actually increases when Joao Pedro is absent, rising from 1.4 chances created per 90 minutes to 1.9. However, his goals return falls from 0.5 per 90 to 0.2, suggesting the striker's presence is more closely linked to Palmer's goalscoring output than his creativity.

The pair have developed a productive partnership. Joao Pedro has assisted four Palmer goals, while Palmer has provided three assists to the ex- Brighton forward..

There is less data available for Rogers given his more recent arrival, but the trend is similar.

Rogers has played 523 Premier League minutes alongside Joao Pedro and 360 without him. With Joao Pedro available, Rogers averages 0.7 goals per 90 minutes and 0.9 goal involvements per 90. Without him, those figures fall to 0.3 goal involvements per 90.

While the sample size remains relatively small, the figures suggest Chelsea 's attacking players generally produce more when Joao Pedro plays.

All three of his assists this season have been for either Rogers or Palmer, sparking early season excitement about Chelsea 's new trio, with nicknames like 'JP Morgan' and 'CPR' having been given to them.

With 20 goals and eight assists, Joao Pedro has been directly involved in 36.4% of Chelsea 's 77 Premier League goals since joining the club.

Whether he is the Blues' most important player remains open to debate.

The statistics do show, however, that their points return with him in the side is consistent with Champions League qualification, whereas their return without him is not.

Alonso's team have yet to demonstrate they can perform at the same level when the Brazilian is unavailable.

articles.title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani Reveals He Tore His Achilles After Suffering Pickup Soccer Injury
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Friday that he tore his Achilles while playing a game of pickup soccer against the NYC press corps on Thursday night.
articles.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Friday that he tore his Achilles while playing a game of pickup soccer against the NYC press corps on Thursday night.

During a press conference regarding his plan to close the Rikers Island jail, Mamdani noted that he scored a goal as part of a 10-5 victory, only to tear his Achilles after he "forgot that [he] was 35."

Sporting crutches and a walking boot, Mamdani declared that he will be in the boot for six to eight weeks and will not be able to play soccer again for another nine months.

articles.title: Sorloth, otro tormento de inicio
articles.standfirst: Le cuesta arrancar todas las temporadas: sin marcar después de 16 partidos del Atlético. En las dos primeras apenas anotó 2 y 4 goles en los 16 primeros.
articles.summary: Le cuesta arrancar todas las temporadas: sin marcar después de 16 partidos del Atlético. En las dos primeras apenas anotó 2 y 4 goles en los 16 primeros.
articles.body: En el foco, ahí está Alexander Sorloth desde hace meses. Primero, por la negativa rojiblanca de darle la salida el pasado verano ante la imposibilidad de conseguir un recambio de garantías. Después, por abrirle la puerta que estaba cerrada a cal y canto de cara a los próximos mercados. Ahora, por su rendimiento deportivo que alcanzó su peor momento en los choques ante Bayern y Barça, el primero siendo titular y el segundo como primer cambio de Simeone. Dos encuentros que aumentaron el particular tormento que vive el noruego, que arrancó la temporada lesionado y que todavía no ha podido estrenarse en el aspecto goleador. Aunque apenas lleva disputados seis de los 16 partidos rojiblancos, lucir el 9 exige un acierto ante la portería contraria que, todavía, no ha llegado. Algo que en cualquier caso no es nuevo para un delantero que sufre en los arranques de temporada. En la campaña 25-26, por ejemplo, en sus 16 primeros partidos había marcado solo dos goles (Celta y Madrid). Terminó con 20 la temporada como máximo goleador del equipo empatado con un Julián que vuelve a estar por delante en la rotación del Cholo y que este curso, con muchos más minutos, apenas lleva dos goles. Una deriva, la de Sorloth, que no es nueva desde que llegó al Atlético. En su estreno marcó ante su ex, el Villarreal, pero aquella temporada 24-25 también tardó en arrancar. En sus 16 primeros partidos marcó 4 (el citado del Villarreal, dos al Leganés y uno a Las Palmas). Terminó con 24 despejando las dudas que siempre aparecen en sus inicios. En estas tres temporadas el 9 lleva cero goles en las cuatro primeras jornadas de Champions. Más allá del choque ante el Getafe, tiene la opción de romper el mal fario precisamente ante equipos de su país. Y es que además del Viking el próximo miércoles dos jornadas después llegará la visita al Bodo, por lo que dos de los tres próximos partidos europeos serán ante equipos de su país. Buena receta para acabar con el tormento de inicio

articles.title: Manchester United fan criticism has gone too far at times - Omar Berrada
articles.summary: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada says some of the recent criticism of the club's hierarchy has "crossed a line".
articles.body:
Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada says some of the criticism aimed at the club's hierarchy has "crossed a line".

In a rare interview to Sky Sports as head coach Mauricio Pochettino prepares for his first game in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday, Berrada said he "understood" the frustration of supporters at United being 18th in the Premier League. He also said some of the criticism was "fair".

However, he feels some of it has gone too far.

"Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we're going to get," he said. "We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.

"We do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that."

United's director of football Jason Wilcox has been singled out by supporters at recent games. There have also been social media calls for both Wilcox and Berrada to lose their jobs.

In addition, songs are now sung regularly calling for minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to leave, while opposition to the Glazer family has remained intense since their leveraged buyout in 2005 saddled debt on to the club that now exceeds £1bn.

Man Utd happy with summer transfers; Pochettino wants say in future deals

Wilcox, in particular, has been blamed for what is perceived to have been poor summer recruitment. After the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in September, defender Lisandro Martinez said he "expected more from the technical director".

Ousted boss Michael Carrick felt he was let down by a transfer strategy that targeted midfield, while not addressing issues at left-back and in attack - which has been compounded by injuries to Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko.

Carrick wanted to target Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes, but United backed off when Nottingham Forest and West Ham's demands went higher than they wanted to pay. Anderson eventually joined Manchester City for £116m, with Fernandes moving to Tottenham for £85m.

Instead, United paid a combined £118m for Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos, who have started seven Premier League games between then, and triggered Youri Tielemans' £35m release clause at Aston Villa. Tielemans scored his first United goal in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on 8 November and has one assist.

However, Berrada has defended United's transfer business, saying: "When we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

"We went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play and we've said consistently in the last few years we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players, for the right value at the right time - in terms of what the squad needs.

"When we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it. So, could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players at the right value.

"There's no point in us spending £40m, £50m for players we're not convinced are going to add value to the team."

When he spoke to the wider media for the first time, 30 minutes before Berrada's interview was aired, Pochettino said he hoped to have a say in all areas of the playing side, even though his official title is head coach.

"I know that, being a head coach, I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday," he said. "I'm going to pick the starting 11 and I'm going to make the changes.

"Of course, in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad."

We have to put Man Utd into a different place - Pochettino

Berrada said there had been little option other than to dismiss Carrick given United's plight and the team had "dropped off in many areas".

Pochettino has spoken individually to virtually every player to get an understanding of what the issues are.

He said he was wary of reading too much into data that shows United's players have not been running enough, arguing "if you don't put context on the data, it's very dangerous to talk".

The 54-year-old also said that, despite talking extensively about culture in his first in-house interview on Thursday, it could take 10 years to build one.

"The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear," he said. "It's a historic club, one of the best in the world. It's difficult to find another club the size of Manchester United.

"The culture of the club and the identity of the club is very clear. It needs to be in a different place than we are now."

Pochettino did confirm Bruno Fernandes will remain as skipper for the trip to Liverpool.

Fernandes has struggled for form and, with the 32-year-old's contract due to expire in the summer, there has been no breakthrough in negotiations over an extension.

United do have the option to trigger an additional year on the Portugal playmaker's present deal but, given the massive dip from the levels that earned him all last season's major player of the year awards, there are some who wonder whether a clean break might be best.

Pochettino preferred to deflect the wider aspect of Fernandes' future and concentrate on the immediate.

"Bruno is our captain and he's a very important player," he said.

"I think we will have time after to talk about the [other] things that you are asking me."

articles.title: Tony Mowbray: Support for Blackburn boss no surprise, says Damien Johnson
articles.summary: Blackburn Rovers interim boss Damien Johnson says the support shown for head coach Tony Mowbray shows the high regard he is held in.
articles.body:
The overwhelming support from the world of football for Blackburn Rovers boss Tony Mowbray has come as no surprise to interim head coach Damien Johnson.

Mowbray announced on Wednesday he was stepping back from his role at the Championship club because of health issues with Johnson and Mike Dodds taking charge "for the time being".

The news sparked an outpouring of messages of support from EFL clubs and further afield.

"To someone like me, it's not a surprise," Johnson said.

"I've known him for over 10 years, but I think people who have only known him in this club for the four or five months he's been in, they can see that. That's just the impact Tony has on people, it's just a testament to Tony and his nature and how he is and how he treats people."

Mowbray, 62, returned to Ewood Park in June for a second spell as head coach and has taken them to 13th place in the Championship after they finished just five points clear of the relegation zone last season.

The former Middlesbrough and West Brom boss had previously taken time out of the game during his spell as Birmingham City boss in early 2024 following a health scare, and later revealed he had been undergoing treatment for bowel cancer.

Boro head coach Kim Hellberg was one of the first to send his best wishes to one of his predecessors.

"He's a brilliant guy. It was really good to meet him and he was absolutely brilliant every time I've talked to him," Hellberg said.

"He's a brilliant football coach. He's done a lot of good things. He's a brilliant human being and you can see everyone knows that."

Rovers have won five of their past nine league games with Johnson crediting Mowbray's impact at the club for creating a more positive atmosphere.

"When the statement came out there was concern - we care a lot about Tony and it was a little bit of a shock - we want what's best for him at this time," Johnson told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"Tony has built a real bond with the whole group and with everyone at the whole club, so there was naturally concern for him and a bit of emotion for a day or so but we all hold him in the highest regard - we hope he's given the privacy he needs.

"He sent a private message to the players which was read out today [Friday] and they appreciated it. He's sent some private messages to staff but Tony's allowed us just to get on, he'll be allowed the time he needs and we'll just get on with the game."

Blackburn visit Burnley on Sunday (12:00 GMT) hoping to end a 10-game winless run against their Lancashire rivals, who have not won a home game in the league since 18 October last year.

Johnson says the match is their main focus rather than what may happen with the managerial situation down the line.

"We've just been focused fully on the game, we know it's a huge game and we've been working with the team throughout the week. The discussions have been about the game and nothing else," he added.

Meanwhile, Blackburn are set to be without goalkeeper Balazs Toth until the new year after he told Hungarian media , external he suffered a hand injury while playing for his national side against Northern Ireland on Tuesday.

"The situation is not that good, but for now it looks like I will be able to avoid surgery," he said before travelling back to England to have the injury assessed by Blackburn.

articles.title: Kalen DeBoer Says Alabama Roster Is Most 'Complete' He's Had Since Taking Over for Nick Saban
articles.summary: Now in his third season at Alabama since replacing Nick Saban, head coach Kalen DeBoer believes this is the best team he has had with the program as the Crimson Tide move closer to securing a spot in the College Football Playoff.
articles.body:
Now in his third season at Alabama since replacing Nick Saban, head coach Kalen DeBoer believes this is the best team he has had with the program as the Crimson Tide move closer to securing a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Speaking to ESPN's Alex Scarborough , DeBoer called this group the most "complete" roster he has had in his tenure at Alabama.

"I feel like we're more complete as a football team and able to play anybody, anytime, anywhere," DeBoer said. "But you got to go do it."

Replacing Saban, who retired in January 2024, was going to be a near-impossible task for anyone who tried. He led the Crimson Tide to 16 consecutive seasons with at least 10 wins from 2008 to '23 and six national titles in 17 seasons.

DeBoer got the gig and started 9-5 through 14 games, including a 1-3 mark between the end of the 2024 season and first game of 2025. The latter result, a 31-17 loss to Florida State, led to analysts digging into his buyout in the event Alabama decided to make a change.

Alabama rebounded to make the College Football Playoff last season, but also lost to Georgia in the SEC Championship Game and Indiana in the CFP quarterfinals by a combined score of 66-10.

This season hasn't been without hiccups for Alabama, notably back-to-back losses to Georgia and Tennessee, but the overall results support DeBoer's claim.

The Crimson Tide are currently No. 3 in the College Football Playoff Top 25. They rank in the top 25 among all FBS teams in both points for and points allowed per game.

DeBoer and Alabama have two games remaining in the regular season against Chattanooga and Auburn. An appearance in the SEC Championship remains on the table, though the tiebreaker scenarios are very complex based on the current standings.

articles.title: Vitor Matos accepts Swansea City fans' anger over shock exit to RC Strasbourg
articles.summary: Vitor Matos addresses his unexpected departure from Swansea City at his first press conference as RC Strasbourg boss.
articles.body:
Vitor Matos admits he knows why Swansea City fans will be angry following his sudden departure from the club.

The Portuguese head coach quit the Championship side this week for the top job at French Ligue 1 club RC Strasbourg.

His move took Swansea by complete surprise, just a week before marking his first year in charge with the club sixth in the table and having signed a new contract until 2030 in July.

Speaking at his first press conference at Strasbourg, Matos admitted he does "not expect any goodwill" from the Welsh club's supporters.

He said: "One situation I need to address is Swansea. It was a really hard and tough decision to leave the club mainly because it was a place from the first day, that treated me with all respect and care – me and my family.

"So it was a really tough decision to leave and that's why I needed to thank everyone there.

"Saying that, I really don't expect any good will from the Swansea supporters after my decision. I understand they are angry with that, but it's a club that I love that I worked every day to make better, me and my staff."

Silly to talk about full-time Swans job - Williams

A badly timed shock - the story of Matos' Swans exit

Swansea are expecting a compensation package of about £5m and have appointed former players Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O'Leary to take temporary charge for Saturday's league fixture against West Bromwich Albion.

"To the staff and to the players I have no doubt they will succeed in the future," said Matos.

"I have no doubt that the manager will go into the office and make the club move forward and fulfil the dreams of the club."

He added: "I'm really proud to be Racing's next manager. This is a wonderful club that deserves all thee respect of everyone."

articles.title: Johnstone Burgh: Scottish fifth-tier club no longer required to play twice in one day
articles.summary: Scottish fifth-tier club Johnstone Burgh are forced to play two cup ties on the same day, with the kick-offs only half an hour apart.
articles.body:
Scottish fifth-tier club Johnstone Burgh will no longer be forced to play two cup ties on the same day after one of the fixtures was postponed.

Johnstone were scheduled to play away to Tayport in the Scottish Communities Cup third round at 14:30 GMT and host Dunipace 65 miles away in the Lowland League Cup first round at 15:00 on Saturday.

However, the tie with Tayport has been called off because of a frozen pitch.

The double engagement came about after neither of Johnstone's opponents, nor any other clubs they were scheduled to play on other weekends, were willing to shift from Saturday afternoon kick-off times.

articles.title: El Madrid juega con 'otro' Mbappé
articles.standfirst: Entre Güler, Bellingham y Diomande replican el espectacular caudal ofensivo del delantero
articles.summary: Entre Güler, Bellingham y Diomande replican el espectacular caudal ofensivo del delantero
articles.body: Tener a Mbappé es tener un tesoro. Son pocos los equipos en el mundo que pueden presumir de tener a un jugador tan diferencial en ataque, un delantero que se eleva cada temporada por encima de las 40 acciones de valor gol con una facilidad y regularidad pasmosa. Así los reflejan sus números en el Real Madrid: 44 goles, cuatro asistencias y cuatro penaltis provocados en su primera temporada de blanco; 42 goles, tres asistencias y otros cuatro penaltis provocados la pasada campaña; y 17 goles, tres asistencias y dos penaltis provocados lleva en el presente año. El impacto ofensivo del delantero francés resulta descomunal. La otra buena noticia en el Real Madrid es que no sólo disfruta de un Mbappé, sino que lo hace de 'dos'. Entre Güler, Bellingham y Diomande replican el espectacular caudal ofensivo de Kylian. Es un tres para uno del que resulta un balance ofensivo similar al que genera Mbappé por sí mismo. Si el 10 blanco ha producido ya con el Real Madrid 22 acciones de valor gol, entre sus tres compañeros han protagonizado 24. Una buena noticia para Mourinho, que amortigua de alguna manera la inevitable dependencia del equipo en un jugador tan demoledor de cara a puerta. Así, Güler, con sus cinco goles y cinco asistencias, Bellingham, cinco y cuatro, y Diomande, cuatro y uno, llegan a superar por poco el balance ofensivo del 10 madridista y se convierten en otras tres armas valiosísimas en ataque para el conjunto madridista, que con ellos disfruta de 'otro' Mbappé en el campo. Los 'dos' Mbappé con los que juega el Real Madrid han sido claves en la racha de ocho victorias consecutivas. El conjunto blanco ha dado un pequeño empujón hacia arriba al listón de su poder ofensivo, a la altura de lo que se espera de un equipo plagado de jugadores con un gran impacto en ataque. El Madrid ha marcado en esta racha triunfal un total de 24 goles (una media de tres por partido), mejorando los 20 goles iniciales que marcó en los primeros ocho partidos de la temporada. Además, esta cifra anotadora del último mes le acerca al Barcelona, que en el mismo periodo de tiempo ha marcado 26 tantos. En el caso de los azulgrana, su registro de cara a puerta se ha debilitado, después de que los de Flick anotasen la increíble cifra de 36 goles en los primeros ocho encuentros de la temporada (una media de 4.5 goles por partido).

articles.body: El ‘mundo Brahim Díaz’ anda hoy algo revolucionado por las informaciones aparecidas sobre la renovación del delantero malagueño por el club blanco, algo que en MARCA ya llevamos anunciando desde hace casi un año. Sea como fuere, el Real Madrid oficializará la próxima semana la renovación de BD hasta 2031, aunque en un principio se había especulado, hace un año, con que este acuerdo iba a ser hasta 2030. Esta renovación viene tras rechazar BD, en los pasados meses, ofertas supermillonarias de varios lugares del mundo. El anuncio oficial de la próxima semana será un 'boom' también en Marruecos, donde el delantero blanco es una auténtica estrella deportiva, publicitaria e incluso social.

articles.title: El impulsivo Gattuso: "Quería dejar el coche y saltar por encima de la puerta, pero preferí no hacer el ridículo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico se encontró un día de esta semana con la entrada al campo de entrenamiento cerrada
articles.summary: El técnico se encontró un día de esta semana con la entrada al campo de entrenamiento cerrada
articles.body: Ni Gattuso se ha podido escapar del estreno mundial del Grand Theft Auto VI, el videojuego que ha cautivado a millones de personas. Muchos futbolistas han mostrado su entusiasmo por poder disfrutar de nuevo del GTA trece años después de la anterior entrega. Uno de ellos es Dele-Bashiru. "Lo descargué ayer, pero aún no he jugado, lo haré hoy", dijo el jugador de la Lazio, que desveló que él y Nuno Tavares eran los más aficionados a la videoconsola del vestuario. A Gattuso le cuestionaron sobre si sería un problema que alguno de sus futbolistas se quedara jugando hasta altas horas de la noche al Grand Theft Auto VI. "Será cosa suya si juega a la PlayStation. Ni siquiera sé que haya salido este juego, no sé de qué estáis hablando. No me planteo este problema. Nunca se me ocurriría ir a un jugador y preguntarle a qué hora se ha ido a dormir o si ha jugado al GTA. Mañana por la mañana, a las nueve, desayunaremos todos juntos. Me pondré allí bien concentrado para ver si alguno se ha quedado despierto hasta altas horas o no", comentó. El entrenador, genio y figura, también desveló una anécdota que le ha ocurrido esta semana cuando al llegar al campo de entrenamiento se encontró con la entrada principal cerrada y tuvo que ingresar por otro acceso. "Como soy supersticioso, pensé en volver a hacerlo esta vez", ha dicho con una sonrisa, al recordar que hace tiempo ya había saltado por encima de una puerta de su casa, que estaba bloqueada, para no llegar tarde a un entrenamiento. Esta vez lo pensó, pero no lo llevó a cabo. "Quería dejar el coche allí delante y saltar la puerta. Pero después preferí evitar hacer el ridículo y entré por otro acceso", explicó ante los periodistas. Ya más en serio, sobre su estancia en la Lazio, equipo al que llegó este verano, reconoció que está muy feliz: "Me encuentro a gusto. Me gustaría quedarme mucho tiempo. Cuando uno llega a un lugar como este, donde se dan todas las condiciones para trabajar bien, es obvio que piense en echar raíces".

articles.title: La intrahistoria del primer golazo del Mundial: “Los pusimos a tirar hasta reventarse las piernas”
articles.standfirst: El misil de falta de Ebrima Tunkara a China fue el fruto de un plan ensayado durante días tras una lección aprendida ante Brasil
articles.summary: El misil de falta de Ebrima Tunkara a China fue el fruto de un plan ensayado durante días tras una lección aprendida ante Brasil
articles.body: Faltaba poco para el descanso en el estreno de España en el Mundial Sub-17 de Catar. El marcador reflejaba un ajustado 1-0, obra de un penalti transformado por Jordi Pesquer, y China, subcampeona de Asia, resistía atrincherada cerca de su área. Entonces Ebrima Tunkara colocó el balón sobre la hierba, cerca de la frontal, tomó carrera y descargó un zurdazo que se coló con potencia, inalcanzable para el guardameta. Un misil tierra-aire que hizo estallar el partido y que, visto desde fuera, parecía pura improvisación de un talento precoz. No lo era. Detrás de aquel fogonazo había semanas de trabajo y una idea nacida, paradójicamente, de una derrota ajena. El propio seleccionador, David Cubillo, se lo reveló a MARCA tras el partido. “Jugamos un torneo en Suiza contra Brasil y, analizándolos, detectamos que sus jugadores metían goles de falta directa, algo que a nosotros nos ha faltado en los últimos campeonatos”, explicó. Lo que vio en los brasileños se convirtió en una asignatura pendiente que España decidió aprobar a base de prueba y error. El método, a simple vista, no esconde mucho misterio. “Elegimos lanzadores y los pusimos a tirar dos días seguidos, hasta reventarse las piernas”, resumió Cubillo, que no obstante se negó a atribuirse ningún mérito sobre el ejecutor: “Yo no le puedo enseñar nada a Ebrima, es un pedazo de futbolista. Por suerte o por casualidad ha entrado, pero tiene un golpeo fantástico; lo que necesita es confianza para repetirlo muchas veces más”. El protagonista coincidió en el diagnóstico y situó el origen del gol en la misma semana de entrenamientos. “Viene de la semana que estuvimos en Madrid. Estuvimos dos o tres días lanzando faltas”, contó Tunkara a MARCA. “Creo que ya le he cogido la práctica; la puse a prueba y salió el resultado”. Una jugada para presentarse al torneo por la puerta grande. El tanto no solo adornó el estreno. Lo condujo a buen puerto. “El 2-0 de Ebrima al final de la primera parte nos abrió el panorama para la segunda”, admitió Cubillo. Con esa renta, España se soltó tras el descanso y firmó una goleada —penalti de Pesquer, el libre de Tunkara, el doblete de Owen Emeka y el cierre de Guillermo Trujillano— que puso un 5-0 a una China que había aguantado media hora antes de derrumbarse.

articles.title: ‘I forgot that I was 35’: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces 9 months out after tearing Achilles in soccer game against journalists

articles.body: Zohran Mamdani managed to get on the scoresheet before his evening of pickup football took an unfortunate turn. The New York City mayor revealed that he had torn his Achilles tendon during a match against the City Hall press corps, joking that he had briefly forgotten his age after scoring early. Now facing several months away from the pitch, the 35-year-old will spend the next six to eight weeks wearing a medical boot.Zohran Mamdani tears Achilles during 10-5 victory over journalistsMamdani disclosed the injury on Friday, November 20, while arriving at a press conference on crutches and wearing a medical boot on his right leg. The event concerned his plan to close Rikers Island jail, but reporters also wanted to know what had happened during Thursday night's friendly football match against members of the New York City press corps.The mayor explained that his team won 10-5, although his personal contribution came with an unfortunate aftermath. He scored shortly after getting onto the pitch before tearing his Achilles during the game."I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35. And soon after, I tore my Achilles," Mamdani said.According to reports, the injury occurred during the second half while he was running towards the ball on an indoor turf field. It was described as a non-contact injury, and Mamdani acknowledged that he had skipped an important part of his preparation."I did not stretch," he said when asked why the injury might have happened.Mamdani, who reportedly arrived late for the match, said he would need to wear the medical boot for six to eight weeks. He expects to be able to play football again in approximately nine months.Mamdani's football interest extends to World Cup and Gotham FC initiativesThe injury interrupts a familiar pastime for a mayor who has remained an enthusiastic football fan during his time in office. Mamdani has regularly played pickup matches and has also pursued initiatives aimed at making major football events more accessible to New Yorkers.With MetLife Stadium in New Jersey hosting matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, his administration negotiated with FIFA to secure 1,000 tickets priced at $50 for New York residents. He has also worked with local National Women's Soccer League club Gotham FC on affordable ticket initiatives, first in April and again for the opening round of the playoffs earlier in November.For now, however, Mamdani's own football schedule will have to wait. articles.title: Ismaila Sarr ready for fresh start at Crystal Palace after Liverpool interest
articles.summary: Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr says he has moved on from Liverpool's interest in signing him and is keen for a "fresh start" under Thomas Frank.
articles.body:
Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr says he has moved on from Liverpool 's interest in signing him and is keen for a "fresh start" under new manager Thomas Frank.

The Senegal international, 28, is keen to put that episode behind him after Liverpool explored a move at the end of the summer transfer window.

Ultimately, Palace rejected advances for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games in all competitions last season as his side won the Conference League, while Liverpool opted to keep Cody Gakpo despite interest from Manchester City.

In his first interview since Liverpool 's pursuit of him, Sarr - who has been nominated for the African footballer of the year award - told BBC Sport: " Liverpool is one of the biggest clubs in world football and, when a club like that shows an interest in you, of course it's something you take seriously.

"I don't think any player would be indifferent to that kind of opportunity. It was an interesting possibility, and naturally, I considered what it could mean for my career.

"Today, that chapter is behind me. I've always believed that you can't move forward if you're constantly looking in the rear-view mirror.

"I'm a Crystal Palace player, I'm proud of what we've achieved together, and my focus is on getting back on the pitch and helping the team."

Sarr is still sidelined with a groin injury, but talks are ongoing with Palace over an improved contract - despite his current deal running until 2029.

He added: "Yes, there have been discussions with the club. For now, I prefer to let those conversations happen privately and concentrate on football."

Sarr missed most of Pierre Sage's spell in charge, making just two brief substitute appearances in the Premier League this season.

"Of course, it's a difficult moment for everyone at the club," Sarr said. "After everything we achieved last season, nobody expected us to be in this position.

"But I know the quality of this squad. We have very good players, a strong group and the ability to turn things around.

"The arrival of Thomas Frank is an opportunity for a fresh start, new energy and a different approach. We all have to take responsibility, work together and fight for every point.

"I'm confident we can overcome this difficult period and achieve our objectives this season."

Sarr hopes award goes to Senegalese player

Sarr is on 10-man shortlist for the African Player of the Year award, which will be presented on 7 December in Lagos, Nigeria.

It follows Sarr being named Conference League Player of the Season, scoring nine goals as Palace won their first European title. He also collected both the club's player of the year and players' player of the year awards.

Sarr went on to score four goals for Senegal at the 2026 World Cup, after featuring in a controversial Africa Cup of Nations final in January.

In March, Senegal's final victory over Morocco was overturned after players left the pitch without the authorisation of the referee.

As Senegal appeal to be reawarded with their title at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), Sarr remains proud that his side "became the African champions on the pitch".

Asked about his chances of winning the African Player of the Year award, he said: "I'm proud of the season I've had, both with Crystal Palace and Senegal. It's been a special year, with important trophies and individual achievements.

"But African football has so many outstanding players, and several of them have also had fantastic seasons.

"I'm thinking particularly of my Senegalese brothers Sadio Mane and Pape Gueye, who also deserve recognition for what they've achieved.

"Of course, winning the award would be an incredible honour. Every African player dreams of that.

"But honestly, what matters most to me is seeing the trophy go to Senegal. I'm incredibly proud of what we accomplished together."

articles.title: Malachi Toney's Return from Injury Teased by Miami's Mario Cristobal Ahead of CFB Playoffs
articles.summary: University of Miami head football coach Mario Cristobal provided a positive injury update Friday on star wide receiver Malachi Toney.
articles.body:
University of Miami head football coach Mario Cristobal provided a positive injury update Friday on star wide receiver Malachi Toney.

During an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show , Cristobal said, "As of yesterday, he was running 19, 20 miles per hour. Probably a little bit more. Yeah, he's really close."

Cristobal went on to say that Toney is "probably a week and a half out."

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on Nov. 4 that Toney was set to undergo surgery to treat a high ankle sprain, and Thamel noted at the time that the timeline for recovery was usually about four weeks.

Toney missed Miami's loss to Notre Dame and win over Duke, plus it sounds as though he will sit out Saturday's home game against Virginia Tech.

However, Cristobal's comments suggest it is not out of the question that Toney could return for the Hurricanes' regular-season finale against Boston College on Nov. 28 or the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5.

Prior to the injury, Toney was enjoying a dominant season that had him in the Heisman Trophy conversation.

In eight games, the dynamic wideout has racked up 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns, representing a great follow-up to his 2025 freshman campaign when he made 109 catches for 1,211 yards and 10 scores.

While being without Toney may have played a big role in Miami's first loss of the season when it fell 31-24 to Notre Dame, the Hurricanes were able to win without him against Duke.

Even if Toney doesn't play again during the regular season, 9-1 Miami will be a big favorite against 6-4 Virginia Tech and 4-6 Boston College.

The competition will get tougher in the ACC Championship Game, though, likely against either 9-1 Wake Forest or 7-3 Louisville.

Should Miami win its last two regular-season games and the ACC Championship Game, it should be in strong position for a first-round bye in the College Football Playoff.

Unless the unexpected happens, Miami should be back in the CFP regardless, one year after making a surprise run to the National Championship Game.

Cristobal's update on Friday suggests Toney should be close to full health by the time the CFP rolls around, and if that is the case, then the combination of Toney and quarterback Darian Mensah will make the Hurricanes a tough out.

articles.title: Francia 'le quita' una estrella a España
articles.standfirst: Anuncia el encuentro de cuartos de final de la Nations League con una imagen de la camiseta de La Roja a la que le falta un Mundial
articles.summary: Anuncia el encuentro de cuartos de final de la Nations League con una imagen de la camiseta de La Roja a la que le falta un Mundial
articles.body: Es sólo un detalle, quizá sin ninguna mala intención, un simple despiste, pero ha llamado mucho la atención y se ha viralizado en las redes sociales. España y Francia, según ha deparado el sorteo de esta mañana, se verán las caras en los cuartos de final de la Nations League el próximo mes de marzo. Hasta ahí todo normal... Sin embargo, la cuenta oficial en X del combinado galo ha anunciado la eliminatoria con una imagen de jugadores de las dos selecciones. Y en el caso de los españoles, la camiseta que aparece sólo tiene una estrella y no las dos que ya luce La Roja en el pecho después de proclamarse campeona del mundo por segunda vez el pasado mes de julio. Un detalle que ha provocado que muchos usuarios de las redes se cuestionen por qué le han 'quitado' un Mundial a España. Precisamente, en el recuerdo de esta eliminatoria de la Nations aparece el reciente duelo de semifinales de la pasada Copa del Mundo en el que La Roja eliminó a los galos y se metió en la final ante Argentina para, posteriormente, levantar el título. Más allá de esta eliminatoria, Francia y España (la ida será el 25 de marzo de 2027 a las 20:45 y la vuelta el 28 a la misma hora) ya conocen qué camino le espera a la que salga victoriosa, que se cruzará con Países Bajos o Portugal, mientras que Alemania o Bélgica lo harán contra Inglaterra o Noruega. Eso ya será el 9 o el 10 de junio de 2027. La final se disputará el 13 de junio. Zidane, el seleccionador francés, valoró el encuentro ante España de los cuartos de la Nations League y se centró en lo que está por venir, no en lo que ocurrió el pasado mes de julio. "No se trata de una revancha de la semifinal del Mundial, sino de una competición diferente con un nuevo grupo. Y el objetivo sigue siendo el mismo: llegar a la Final Four y ganar la Nations League", comentó.

articles.title: Cristiano marca el 986, luego falla un penalti... y Al Nassr pierde el 'Clásico'
articles.standfirst: El crack portugués mandó una pena máxima al poste para poner a su equipo con 0-2
articles.summary: El crack portugués mandó una pena máxima al poste para poner a su equipo con 0-2
articles.body: Al Nassr perdió una gran oportunidad de ponerse líder provisional de la Saudi Pro League tras perder 3-1 el Clásico de este país ante Al Ahli, campeón asiático, por culpa, en parte del penalti fallado por Cristiano con 0-1 en el marcador, gol marcado antes por el luso. Es el tercer penalti fallado por Cristiano de los últimos cuatro intentados. El partido empezó así de fuerte, con un gran protagonismo de Cristiano Ronaldo. El portugués ponía su gol número 986 de su carrera (noveno en esta Liga) tras un robo de Samu Costa que resolvió Cris a primer toque. Era el 0-1. Ahí no quedó la cosa. Cinco minuto más tarde, Cristiano mandó al poste ese penalti claro a favor de su equipo, pitado por el argentino Facundo Tello. Era el posible 0-2. Y no, se quedó en 0-1. Al Ahli, desde entonces, empezó a despertar. Con mucha marejada en los despachos (suena como director deportivo el del Villarreal MA Tena y sonaba la destitución de su entrenador Marino Pusic), Al Ahli se sobrepuso a todo y marcó un gol... con polémica anulación por falta al portero de Al Nassr (minuto 31). Se quedó la cosa en 0-1. El 1-1 sí fue válido tras el golazo de Galeno desde 30 metros. Ese 1-1 vino en el descuento del primer tiempo. Y a partir de ahí, malas noticias para Al Nassr y para su entrenador, Postecoglou, que está en la cuerda floja: el gol del 'pichichi' (13 goles) Ivan Toney en el 71', merced a un penalti, puso a Al Nassr con la derrota (2-1) y le dejó sin liderato provisional. Luego vino la puntilla, con un córner rematado por Rober Ibáñez (3-1). Al Nassr se queda tercero en la tabla, empatado con el segundo (Al Qadsiah) y dos puntos menos que el líder, Hilal, que tiene, además, un partido por jugar. Al Ahli es cuarto.

Los jugadores y García Plaza se acercaron a los aficionados, y a la salida de autobús se abrió la puerta para que Kike Salas e Isaac Romero, megáfono en mano, arengaran a una entregada hinchada blanquirroja.

articles.title: Liverpool: Virgil van Dijk uncertain on Anfield future beyond the summer but believes he can play for 'many more years'
articles.summary: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk is out of contract in the summer and told Sky Sports he has "no idea" where he will be playing next season; Watch Liverpool vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Premier League on Sunday from 4pm; kick-off 4.30pm.
articles.body:
The 35-year-old centre-back, who has won two Premier League titles and the Champions League during his time at Liverpool, is out of contract in the summer.

He told Sky Sports that, currently, he is uncertain on what will happen beyond this campaign.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," he said.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the new year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a big part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

"If it's getting extended, we'll see then.

"If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

Asked about how emotional that exit would be, he said: " Well, yeah, probably for me the most and the family because it's been an incredible time.

"But I don't look too far in the future and that's been, in my opinion, also a little bit of a success. I won't change it now either.

Van Dijk on his partnership with 'outstanding' Jacquet

Van Dijk has made a positive start to this season, partly thanks to his encouraging connection with new centre-back partner Jeremy Jacquet.

The Dutchman has been impressed by his young team-mate and says they have been working together on and off the pitch to build up their relationship and help each other perform to the highest level.

"He's been outstanding so far I must say," said Van Dijk when asked about Jacquet. "Very young but he plays like a very mature player. He's still 21, he's still going to get so much better and that's a good thing.

"Obviously, I speak to him a lot during the game but after the game and training and certain moments as well where I feel like I can help him.

"As a centre-back partnership, you have to be able to understand what your qualities and what your flaws are at times and then complement each other on those things. You only get there by playing games.

"It's been good because he's helping me, I help him and that's how it should be. I must say I'm impressed with how we started and now it's down to him to keep that level, keep that consistency, stay calm because you can easily get carried away because there's a lot of plaudits coming his way and rightly so. But I know how it can work when you have maybe one lesser game or not up to the standard that you have.

"He just has to keep going, keep staying important and be fit and then things will be working out pretty well."
